name: Shem
overview: Shem, one of Noah's three sons, is prominently featured in the Genesis narrative as a key figure preserved in the ark during the flood (Genesis 7:13, 9:18). Scripture highlights his respectful and honorable conduct toward his father, as he, along with Japheth, covered Noah's nakedness without looking upon it, demonstrating filial reverence (Genesis 9:23). Shem is also noted for his descendants, marking him as an important patriarchal figure in biblical history (Genesis 5:32, 6:10). The variations in his name, such as Sem or SEM in the Authorized Version, reflect the transmission of his legacy through Scripture.
